newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Strike begins at Brazil's Paranagua port - union.
newsitem.headline: Strike begins at Brazil's Paranagua port - union.

text.p: A strike by portworkers at the key Brazilian port of Paranagua begun at 1200 local/1500 GMT as scheduled, a spokesman for the Paranagua Unions Council said.

Talks between dockworkers and port operators continued over dockworkers' demand for a 21 percent pay increase, but any agreement would only result in an end to the strike at 1200 local time Thursday, the spokesman said.
"There is no way they can call off the strike now. Only at 1200 tomorrow," he said.
The port authority said all activity involving general cargo, including orange juice, wood and cotton, would be halted by the strike.
But shipments of soybeans, soymeal and corn would not be affected as these were via an export terminal which was largely automated and could be operated by just five people.
Loading of soybeans and soymeal would also continue at private terminals and at the export terminal.
The port authority declined to put a figure on the daily cost of the strike to the port.
